description: cbcg.me serves the same content under many differing first path segments (/me/, /r/, /c/, /e/, /en/, /eng/, /images/, /uploads/, /legal/, /discover/, /index/ and even /kursna_lista_arhiva.php/...). Search engines index these variants interchangeably.

result.result_summary: The same page (e.g. registar banaka, tarife banaka) was returned under at least three different prefixes across searches. A fetch of https://www.cbcg.me/r/mapa-sajta returned HTTP 404 although the sitemap page is indexed.

why_it_matters: Hardcoded deep URLs will rot and produce false 'dead source' verdicts. Collection must resolve links dynamically from section roots, and the verifier should treat a single 404 on a prefixed URL as a prefix problem, not a dead source.

description: No open-data API, SDMX endpoint, or bulk-download facility for CBCG banking/payments data was found in either language.

result.result_summary: All observed outputs are HTML pages plus PDF/ZIP/XLS attachments; no /api, data portal, or SDMX reference surfaced in searches.

why_it_matters: Collection must be crawl-and-parse (PDF/XLS extraction), which is slower and more brittle; budget for document parsing rather than API ingestion.

description: Searched in Montenegrin for a CBCG-hosted central repository of bank Pillar 3 disclosures ('objelodanjivanje podataka kreditnih institucija').

result.result_summary: Found the regulatory basis (Odluka o adekvatnosti kapitala banke; a decision on public disclosure of credit-institution data) but no single CBCG page aggregating banks' Pillar 3 disclosure documents. The obligation appears to sit with each bank's own website.

why_it_matters: Pillar 3 capital/risk disclosures likely have to be collected bank-by-bank from institution websites (a different coverage cell), not from CBCG. This is a real structural gap, not a search failure.

description: The fetched 'Finansijski izvještaji banaka' page rendered only a subset of institutions (six banks) although the register lists ~12 active banks.

result.result_summary: Fetch returned CKB, Hipotekarna, Podgorička, Invest banka Montenegro (in liquidation), Prva banka, Erste. NLB, Addiko, Universal Capital, Lovćen, Zapad, Ziraat, Adriatic were not visible in the fetched rendering.

why_it_matters: Likely pagination/JS rendering rather than missing filings — but a naive single-fetch crawler would silently under-collect. Collection must paginate or render JS and reconcile against the bank register.

description: The payment-services/e-money statistics sub-page URL was inferred from navigation labels observed on the parent statistics page, not directly fetched.

result.result_summary: Path '/podaci-o-platnim-uslugama-i-elektronskom-novcu' appeared as a navigation sibling; exact absolute URL not confirmed.

why_it_matters: Flagged with low confidence so the deterministic verification pass resolves the canonical URL from the parent hub rather than assuming it is dead.

description: Ziraat Bank Montenegro's Serbian homepage (ziraatbank.me/sr) as fetched exposes only 'obavještenja' (notices, tariffs, general terms) and no navigation link to a financial-reports or objelodanjivanje section; the annual-reports page was only reachable via a site-scoped search engine query.

result.result_summary: Deep page https://www.ziraatbank.me/sr/godisnji-izvjestaji exists per search index but is not discoverable from the homepage fetch.

why_it_matters: A homepage-only crawler would score Ziraat as a non-disclosing bank, which is wrong. Deep-link seeds are required per bank.

description: https://www.ckb.me/about-us/welcome-to-ckb/reports failed with a TLS error ('unable to verify the first certificate'), and https://www.hipotekarnabanka.com/izvjestaji/javno-objelodanjivanje-podataka returned HTTP 404 while the parent https://www.hipotekarnabanka.com/izvjestaji/ fetched cleanly and lists the disclosure documents.

result.result_summary: Both are hypotheses, not verdicts: CKB is presumed live behind a broken cert chain; the Hipotekarna disclosure sub-path has most likely moved into the consolidated /izvjestaji/ listing (site appears to have migrated to WordPress).

why_it_matters: Recording these as dead would drop the two largest domestic disclosure archives from the collection plan.

description: Searches using the Basel term 'Stub 3' / 'Pillar 3' in Serbian returned no Montenegrin bank hits.

result.result_summary: Montenegrin banks label prudential disclosures 'javno objelodanjivanje podataka' or 'javno objavljivanje podataka' (Art. 237, Zakon o kreditnim institucijama), not Pillar 3/Stub 3.

why_it_matters: Query sets built on Basel vocabulary will systematically miss ME prudential disclosures; the two spelling variants (objelodanjivanje vs objavljivanje) must both be used.

description: A combined multi-bank query for 2025 disclosures (Universal Capital, Adriatic, Lovćen, Ziraat) returned only generic Montenegrin open-data and freedom-of-information results.

result.result_summary: Multi-actor queries dilute; per-bank site-scoped queries were required and worked.

why_it_matters: Sets the query design rule for the collection routine: one bank per query, local-language term + domain.

description: No Montenegrin bank in this cell was observed to operate an 'Investor Relations' section in the Western sense (IR calendar, earnings call, analyst deck, IR contact).

result.result_summary: Disclosure is statutory-document publication under 'O nama', 'Izvještaji', 'Mediji i publikacije' or 'Odnosi sa javnošću' — not an IR function.

why_it_matters: Searching 'investor relations' in English will under-recover this market; navigate by 'izvještaji', 'o nama', 'odnosi sa javnošću' instead. No earnings-call transcripts should be expected as a source type.

description: Direct fetch of the CRPS public search portal (http://www.pretraga.crps.me/) failed with an OpenSSL TLSV1_ALERT_INTERNAL_ERROR when the request was upgraded to HTTPS.

result.result_summary: Could not retrieve the page body; the field structure of the public search form and result pages remains undocumented in this slice. The domain appears repeatedly in current search results, so the hypothesis is a legacy/misconfigured TLS stack or bot defence, not a dead site.

why_it_matters: Any automated collector against CRPS will need a tolerant TLS client (or plain HTTP) and should not be designed assuming a modern HTTPS endpoint.

description: Searched in Montenegrin for a public, free search interface over FILED annual financial statements held by the tax authority (terms: 'pretraga finansijskih iskaza', 'javna objava finansijskih iskaza', 'pregled finansijskih iskaza').

result.result_summary: Only the filing-side portal (eprijava.tax.gov.me/TaxisPortal) and the desktop filing application were found; no evidence of a free public per-company statement lookup equivalent to Serbia's APR or Croatia's RGFI. Commercial redistributors (bilansi.me, boniteti.me, companywall.me) fill this gap, which is itself indirect evidence that no free public search exists.

why_it_matters: Entity-level ME financial statements likely require paid vendors or FOI requests; a scraping-first collection design would fail.

description: Looked for an official CRPS API, bulk download or open-data dump of the company register.

result.result_summary: No official API or bulk endpoint surfaced. Machine-readable access appears to exist only via third parties (OpenCorporates register #168, CompanyData.com) rather than from the registry itself.

why_it_matters: Determines build-vs-buy for the ME entity spine and adds licence cost/terms as a dependency.

description: Searched MONSTAT in Montenegrin for a dedicated structural-business-statistics or financial-institutions release page (terms: 'strukturne poslovne statistike', 'finansijsko posredovanje', 'finansijske institucije').

result.result_summary: MONSTAT's business-register methodology and general publication/yearbook pages were located, but no specific landing page for NACE-K financial-activity aggregates was confirmed. Most ME financial-sector aggregates appear to originate with the central bank rather than MONSTAT.

why_it_matters: Sector aggregates for banking/payments may have to be taken from CBCG (a different coverage cell) with MONSTAT used only for enterprise counts and business demography.

description: The Register of Beneficial Owners at efirma.tax.gov.me is described as searchable, but sources also say registration and extract-ordering require a registered digital certificate.

result.result_summary: Could not determine from public pages whether anonymous public search of UBO records is available or whether all lookups are certificate-gated.

why_it_matters: Ownership-chain analysis for unlisted ME payment firms may require a Montenegrin digital certificate or a local partner.

description: None of the core supranational assessors in this cell (IMF, World Bank, EBRD, EIB, MONEYVAL) appear to publish their Montenegro financial-sector assessments in Montenegrin/Serbian. Searches using sr terms returned only national-media relays and the EU-funded eu.me portal, never an official sr-language version of an Article IV report, Transition Report assessment or MONEYVAL MER.

result.result_summary: Local-language coverage of this cell is effectively second-hand: sr-language material exists only as journalism, government press releases, or EU-info-portal explainers.

why_it_matters: Any sr-language monitoring for this cell must target relays and national counterparts, not the assessors themselves; and translation drift in media relays is a real accuracy risk.

description: The only Montenegro FSAP material located dates to the joint IMF/World Bank FSAP mission of September 2015 (technical notes published around January 2016). No evidence of a newer FSAP or FSAP Update for Montenegro was found in the searches performed.

result.result_summary: FSAP-grade payments/supervision diagnostics for Montenegro are roughly a decade old.

why_it_matters: The deepest structural view of Montenegro's payment infrastructure predates SEPA accession and TIPS-Clone plans, so Article IV annexes and EC Chapter 9 sections must carry that analytical load instead.

description: A dedicated MONEYVAL Montenegro country landing page URL was not isolated in these searches; individual reports were reached via the general evaluations page, plenary-outcome news items, and direct rm.coe.int document links whose slugs are opaque.

result.result_summary: Report discovery for MONEYVAL depends on plenary news pages rather than a predictable per-country document index.

why_it_matters: Automated collection needs a crawler over plenary outcome pages plus rm.coe.int link extraction, not a simple country-page poll.

description: Searches repeatedly surfaced the Central Bank of Montenegro annual report (cbcg.me) and gov.me ERP pages as the national counterparties of these supranational assessments; they are national actors and therefore belong to other coverage cells, not this one.

result.result_summary: Not recorded as candidates here to avoid duplicating another cell's scope.

why_it_matters: Cross-cell linkage matters: supranational recommendations should be joined to CBCG/gov.me implementation documents during analysis.

description: Vijesti (vijesti.me), the largest independent Montenegrin daily and explicitly named in this coverage cell, did not surface a single article in any of seven searches, including two site-scoped local-language queries using its own domain and bank names.

result.result_summary: Only the homepage URL could be established. No economy-section path, article URL pattern, or feed was confirmed. Competing dailies (Dan) and portals (CdM, RTCG) surfaced normally on identical query shapes.

why_it_matters: If Vijesti is systematically absent from the search index available to this run, keyword-based discovery will silently under-represent the outlet most likely to break bank-fee and supervision stories. Collection must be built by direct site crawl, not search.

description: Targeted queries for 'Portal Analitika' (portalanalitika.me) and 'Standard' (standard.co.me) as Montenegrin economy/banking outlets returned no direct hits.

result.result_summary: Neither outlet produced a confirmed URL or banking article in this run; one search summary explicitly noted the absence of Portal Analitika and Standard.co.me results.

why_it_matters: Both are commonly cited Montenegrin portals. Their absence is more likely a search-coverage artefact than evidence they are inactive, so they should be probed directly rather than written off — recording them as candidates now would be fabrication.

description: Local-language searches on payment-fee increases and card pricing ('naknade banaka Crna Gora poskupljenje platne kartice') returned mostly regulator and bank-own material (CBCG fee-comparability pages, CKB general terms PDF, Prva banka card page) rather than press coverage.

result.result_summary: Only two genuine press items on fee increases were found (RTCG 'Banke povećale naknade i provizije'; MINA on fee and commission income), both dated rather than current.

why_it_matters: Payment-fee changes are a core topic for this cell but Montenegrin media appear to cover them episodically, not systematically. Press monitoring alone will miss most fee events; it must be paired with the CBCG fee-comparability register and bank tariff pages, which sit outside this cell.

description: Ekonomist.me, described in reference material as a Podgorica-based finance/fintech magazine founded in 2014, could not be confirmed at a specific live URL in this run.

result.result_summary: The publication was described only via an encyclopedic entry; no article URL or homepage hit appeared in search results. The domain recorded on the candidate is inferred from the publication name and flagged as a hypothesis.

why_it_matters: It is potentially the only dedicated fintech/payments outlet in the market — the single most on-topic source for the payments half of the brief — so confirming or replacing it should be a priority in the verification pass.

description: No paywall, robots.txt, or terms-of-use check was performed on any candidate; access_status values are inferences from search snippets only.

result.result_summary: MINA's full wire service, eKapija premium items, and Bloomberg Adria are the three most likely to be gated, but none was tested. No fetch was attempted against any candidate in this run.

why_it_matters: Collection-method recommendations assume open access. If MINA or eKapija are licence-gated, the effective early-signal channel narrows to Bankar.me, Investitor.me and RTCG, changing the collection design.

description: Udruženje banaka Crne Gore (Association of Banks of Montenegro) — no official website URL was surfaced by search. Only third-party references were found: an NGO registry entry (nvoinfo.me) and media mentions of its officers (Mladen Rabrenović as president, Bratislav Pejaković as secretary general) and of a 'traditional banking conference'.

result.result_summary: Association is confirmed to exist and to co-organise the CBCG FinTech Hackathon, but its own conference agenda/sponsor pages could not be located in this pass.

why_it_matters: It is the most likely publisher of ME-specific banking conference agendas and sponsor lists — the core artefact of this cell. Missing it leaves a hole in domestic event coverage.

description: No dedicated public careers/vacancy pages were surfaced for NLB Banka Podgorica, Hipotekarna banka, Erste Bank Montenegro or Lovćen banka. Searches returned Wikipedia entries, bank-profile aggregators and (for Hipotekarna) only a LinkedIn company page.

result.result_summary: Career-page coverage of ME banks is currently confirmed only for CKB and Prva banka.

why_it_matters: Hiring signals from the second- and third-largest banks are missing, and LinkedIn — the apparent fallback channel — is ToS-restricted for automated collection.

description: No Montenegro-specific 'best digital bank' award programme was found. All award signals located are international programmes (Global Finance, Euromoney, The Banker) with a Montenegro country category, reported through ME media.

result.result_summary: Domestic digital-banking award ecosystem appears absent or not web-visible.

why_it_matters: Means award-based weak signals must be sourced from international award bodies plus local press, not from a national awards body.

description: CBCG FinTech Hackathon editions confirmed for 2021 and 2022 only; no evidence surfaced of editions after 2022 in this pass. A UDG announcement page carries an odd '2028' slug that was not verified.

result.result_summary: The hackathon may be dormant; treat the channel as possibly historical until a recent edition is confirmed.

why_it_matters: Affects whether this is a live monitoring feed or an archival source.

description: LinkedIn (company pages, job posts, INFINTECH showcase) is the richest single weak-signal channel for this cell but is partially login-walled and its terms of service prohibit automated scraping.

result.result_summary: Collectable only via analyst review or a licensed data arrangement.

why_it_matters: Any pipeline design that assumes scraped LinkedIn hiring data is legally and operationally unsound.

description: Search snapshots of ZZZCG indicated zero currently listed vacancies, and ZZZCG has published notices about changes to how vacancies are advertised.

result.result_summary: The public vacancy feed may be thin, paginated behind a form, or partly migrated; volume must be validated before relying on it.

why_it_matters: Could produce false 'no hiring activity' conclusions if the feed is simply not fully exposed.

description: Searched in Montenegrin and English for a dedicated financial ombudsman / alternative dispute resolution body for banking and payments in Montenegro (terms: finansijski ombudsman, ombudsman za bankarske usluge, vansudsko rješavanje sporova korisnika finansijskih usluga).

result.result_summary: No dedicated financial ombudsman was found. The general human-rights Ombudsman (Zaštitnik ljudskih prava i sloboda) has no banking-specific mandate and explicitly no jurisdiction over courts; complaint escalation instead runs bank internal complaint body -> CBCG Service for the Protection of Users of Financial Services.

why_it_matters: Rules out a source class that exists in neighbouring markets and concentrates complaint-channel collection on CBCG plus the consumer NGO CEZAP; also means no published individual complaint decisions naming banks.

description: Searched (sr and en) for an interchange-fee or card-scheme dispute, court case or competition proceeding in Montenegro (interchange naknada spor, međubankarska naknada, Visa, Mastercard, sudski postupak).

result.result_summary: No dispute, AZZK case or judgment on interchange was located. Only the statutory framework surfaced — a Law on interbank fees and special rules for payment card operations reported as Official Gazette of Montenegro no. 145/21 — plus bank card tariff PDFs.

why_it_matters: The adversarial payments-economics detail this cell is meant to harvest appears not to exist yet in Montenegro; card economics must instead be reconstructed from the statute, bank tariff sheets and CBCG fee-comparability disclosures.

description: Attempted to find a standalone published CBCG annual report on consumer/user protection with complaint counts by bank.

result.result_summary: CBCG pages state that data on complaints, their merit and measures taken are compiled and that a bylaw sets reporting deadlines, and the CBCG Annual Report contains a consumer-protection chapter, but no separate per-bank complaint statistics report URL was found in this pass. Unverified whether such a standalone publication exists.

why_it_matters: Per-institution complaint counts are the highest-value item in this cell; if unpublished, an access-to-information request (slobodan pristup informacijama) may be the only route.

description: Searched for AZZK decisions specifically concerning Montenegrin banks or payment institutions.

result.result_summary: Bank-related material found on azzk.me is largely cross-border (e.g. an older Societe Generale Banka Srbije / KBC Banka Beograd concentration PDF) and 2024 lists reportedly include NLB/Addiko and Alta Pay Group/Addiko items, but no domestic Montenegrin bank merger decision text was directly opened and confirmed in this pass.

why_it_matters: The volume of genuinely Montenegro-specific banking merger decisions may be small; expectations for this channel should be calibrated before building heavy collection.

description: Court decision databases on sudovi.me were identified but their search/filter capabilities and full-text coverage for competition and banking matters were not exercised in this pass.

result.result_summary: Listing URLs exist (/uscg/odluke/, /sdvi/odluke, /pscg) but it is unverified whether decisions are full-text searchable, anonymised, or only partially published.

why_it_matters: Determines whether court/enforcement notices can be systematically collected or only sampled.

description: The canonical hostname of Montenegro's open data portal could not be confirmed. Searches surfaced gov.me articles announcing a new 'Open Data Portal' but returned Croatia's data.gov.hr rather than a working data.gov.me; no ME portal landing URL was directly observed.

result.result_summary: gov.me announcement pages found; portal hostname unverified (data.gov.me is a hypothesis, not a finding).

why_it_matters: Open-data portal is the main machine-readable alternative to rotating institutional PDFs; without the right host, dataset harvesting cannot be automated.

description: No domestic or sr-language credit-rating agency covering Montenegrin banks was found. Searches on 'agencija za rejting Crna Gora banka ocjena izvještaj' returned no national CRA; ME coverage appears to come solely from international agencies publishing in English.

result.result_summary: No ME-domiciled or sr-language CRA identified.

why_it_matters: All rating-based verification for ME banks depends on paywalled English-language international agencies, raising cost and access risk.

description: No public S&P/Moody's/Fitch rating was found for individual Montenegrin banks (CKB, Hipotekarna banka, NLB Banka Podgorica, Erste Bank Podgorica). Coverage found was sovereign-level plus parent-group level.

result.result_summary: Bank-level ME ratings not evidenced in open sources this run.

why_it_matters: Bank-level credit opinions may simply not exist for ME subsidiaries; collection design should rely on parent-group reports and CBCG supervisory data instead.

description: Montenegroberza's issuer-disclosure archive structure was not directly observed; the exchange URL was inferred from third-party references (SeeCapitalMarkets) rather than fetched.

result.result_summary: Exchange as a disclosure archive is a strong hypothesis, unconfirmed.

why_it_matters: If the exchange keeps a durable filings archive it is the single best non-web-archive fallback for listed ME banks.

description: The widely cited domain 'montenegroberza.com' is NOT the Montenegro Stock Exchange. Fetching https://www.montenegroberza.com/ returned an unrelated commercial investing-content site with sections 'Frontier Markets', 'RWA & Tokenization', 'Equities & ETFs', 'Offshore Access' and a guest-post/contributor solicitation — a classic expired-domain repurposing. Wikipedia and several aggregators still list it as the official site.

result.result_summary: The real exchange domain is mnse.me (confirmed independently via company-registry and chamber-of-commerce contact records showing info@mnse.me and @mnse.me staff addresses, and by fetching https://www.mnse.me/ which served live Montenegroberza trading data dated 25/08/2026).

why_it_matters: Any collector seeded from Wikipedia or a stale link list would silently ingest SEO content as if it were exchange disclosure. This must be hard-blocklisted in the source registry.

description: The Montenegroberza site (mnse.me) has a flat, minimal navigation — Dobrodošli / Simboli / Vijesti / Kontakt. There is no separate 'Obavještenja emitenata' or 'Izvještaji emitenata' section distinct from the general Vijesti feed.

result.result_summary: Issuer material-event notices, listing-committee decisions and exchange notices are all mixed into a single /code/navigate.asp?Id=122 stream, and per-issuer disclosure history must be reconstructed by filtering that stream on issuer name/symbol.

why_it_matters: Collection design cannot rely on a per-issuer disclosure index; it needs entity resolution over free-text Montenegrin announcement titles, which raises extraction cost and recall risk for bank-specific events.

description: CRPI (Centralni registar propisanih informacija, crpi.me), referenced from the KTK site as the central storage mechanism for regulated information, rendered only a bare 'CRPI Portal' header with no navigable content or search. The www.crpi.me host additionally presented a TLS certificate whose SANs cover only scmnreporting.me hostnames (iam./portal./sp./www.), and https://www.scmnreporting.me/ returned HTTP 404 at the root.

result.result_summary: No public, searchable central repository of Montenegrin listed-issuer regulated information could be reached in this pass. Status is UNVERIFIED — hosts are live and certificates valid, so this reads as an auth gate or wrong entry path, not a dead service.

why_it_matters: This would be the single highest-value source in the cell if accessible: one canonical feed of periodic reports, inside information and major-holdings notifications for all listed banks. Its absence forces reconstruction from the exchange feed plus individual bank websites, which is lossier and slower.

description: CKDD (the CSD) publishes issuer, trading-symbol and debt-securities registers, but its shareholder services page states that shareholder lists are prepared on request of a security owner or a group of owners entitled to inspect the list, against a price list. No public shareholder/ownership search interface was found.

result.result_summary: Detailed shareholder structure for Montenegrin listed banks is request-gated and likely fee-bearing, not open data.

why_it_matters: Shareholder structure is one of the three explicit targets of this coverage cell. Ownership-change tracking must therefore be built indirectly — from exchange block-trade and material-event notices, KTK prospectus documents, bank annual reports and trade press — with a known recall gap.

description: No RSS/Atom feed, JSON API, or bulk-download endpoint was observed on either mnse.me or scmn.me for issuer announcements. mnse.me is a legacy classic-ASP application using query-string navigation (navigate.asp?Id=NNN&newsId=NNN / &stockId=NNN); scmn.me publishes registers only as dated-filename .xls files and documents as PDFs under /images/.

result.result_summary: All collection in this cell must be HTML/PDF/XLS scraping with custom change detection; no vendor-grade feed exists.

why_it_matters: Sets realistic engineering expectations and argues for filename/ID-diffing strategies plus document hashing to avoid duplicate ingestion across mirror domains (e.g. hipotekarnabanka.com vs hb.co.me vs ftp.hb.co.me).

description: The mnse.me homepage displayed a MONEX index value dated 31 December 2010 alongside live 25 August 2026 trading prices and market capitalisation.

result.result_summary: Parts of the exchange site carry stale or mis-labelled reference values.

why_it_matters: Freshness validation and per-field date extraction are mandatory when ingesting mnse.me; naive scraping would mix a 2010 index level into a 2026 time series.

description: Attempting the detail-page pattern https://www.mnse.me/code/navigate.asp?Id=122&newsId=1 returned 'Podaci ne postoje' (data does not exist).

result.result_summary: News IDs are not densely enumerable from 1; historical back-fill by brute-force ID walking is unreliable.

why_it_matters: Archive back-fill for issuer announcements must harvest IDs from paginated list pages (or a web-archive crawl) rather than enumerating the ID space.

description: The exchange offers an EN toggle (/code/navigate.asp?Id=125, index.asp?jezik=en) but the underlying announcement content observed remained in Montenegrin/Serbian. KTK maintains parallel /en/ paths, though issuer documents (prospectuses, registers) are Montenegrin-only.

result.result_summary: English-language search alone would have surfaced almost none of the operative disclosure surface for this cell.

why_it_matters: Confirms that local-language collection and NLP (Montenegrin/Serbian, both Latin and Cyrillic-tolerant) is mandatory for this cell rather than optional.

description: Searched in Serbian/Montenegrin for a domestically licensed card processor or standalone acquirer ('kartično poslovanje', 'procesiranje kartica', 'Multicard', 'Digital Systems') and found no Montenegro-domiciled dedicated card-processing company with its own disclosure surface.

result.result_summary: Card processing in ME appears to be delivered by banks (notably CKB/OTP, Hipotekarna) and by regional vendors (Payten/Asseco SEE, Monri) rather than by a locally licensed standalone processor. Searches returned only unrelated hardware retailers for 'procesori'.

why_it_matters: The cell's 'card processors and acquirers' half must be tracked indirectly through bank acquiring pages and regional vendor announcements; expecting local processor disclosures would leave a permanent blind spot.

description: The CBCG e-money institution register page states that no e-money institution is currently entered.

result.result_summary: 'U Registru trenutno nema upisane institucije za elektronski novac' observed on the register page.

why_it_matters: There is currently no ME-licensed EMI population to monitor; e-money activity, if any, arrives via banks or EU-passported entities. The register should be treated as a tripwire rather than a data feed.

description: Searched for press releases / 'saopštenja' from the licensed ME payment institutions (Payspot ME, Alta Pay Group, Moneta MNE, Prestopay, Capital Transfer MNE, Business Integration and Business Intelligence).

result.result_summary: No dedicated press-release or investor-relations sections were located for these entities; several (Prestopay, Business Integration and Business Intelligence, Moneta MNE) returned no identifiable corporate website at all. Capital Transfer MNE's only visible channel is social media.

why_it_matters: Corporate-disclosure coverage for ME payment institutions cannot rely on IR pages; it must lean on the CBCG register PDFs, CRPS filings and local news pickup.

description: A fetch of the tariff-overview parent path returned HTTP 404 while its child path /tarife-banaka appears in search results and in-site navigation.

result.result_summary: https://www.cbcg.me/me/kljucne-funkcije/platni-promet/pregledi-tarifa-pruzalaca-platnih-usluga returned 404 on a single attempt; the section is very likely live under language-prefixed or child paths (me/, eng/, r/, legal/ variants observed).

why_it_matters: Recorded as unverified rather than dead, per the rule that one failed fetch is a hypothesis. The verification pass should probe the language-prefix variants before marking anything broken.

description: Searched for annual reports / earnings disclosures by ME payment institutions and e-money issuers.

result.result_summary: None of the seven registered payment institutions is listed on the Montenegro Stock Exchange or publishes annual reports publicly; financial statements are reachable only via CRPS/Tax Administration filings.

why_it_matters: The run topics 'annual reports', 'investor relations' and 'earnings' have essentially no direct surface in this cell; CRPS becomes the mandatory substitute and should be prioritised in collection design.

description: No dedicated Montenegro-specific Visa or Mastercard newsroom/press-release site was found. Visa serves ME via the regional visasoutheasteurope.com country subtree and Mastercard via the Serbian-language mastercard.rs 'Crna Gora' pages and global newsroom filters.

result.result_summary: Searches in both sr and en returned scheme marketing/product pages, FAQs and a Facebook page (MastercardCG), not a country press office feed.

why_it_matters: Scheme country announcements for ME must be harvested from regional/global newsrooms with keyword filters rather than a country feed; expect low recall and latency for ME-specific items.

description: No national card switch / domestic card scheme or shared card-processing house for Montenegro was identified.

result.result_summary: Local-language search for 'procesor kartica / obrada kartičnih transakcija Crna Gora' returned only consumer-electronics retailers and unrelated pages; no evidence of a domestic card scheme analogous to DinaCard.

why_it_matters: Suggests ME card processing is handled by international schemes and bank/third-party processors abroad, so the card-infrastructure signal must be tracked via issuers, schemes and CBCG statistics rather than a national switch operator.

description: Reported instant-payment transaction caps differ across sources (EUR 1,000 per transaction in law-amendment coverage vs EUR 3,000 per transaction in go-live coverage).

result.result_summary: Draft-law reporting cited a 1,000 EUR cap and 10-second execution; go-live reporting cited a 3,000 EUR cap and 5-cent fee ceiling for transfers up to 200 EUR.

why_it_matters: Parameter values must be sourced from the CBCG instant-payment rulebook/decision, not from press; secondary-source figures should be treated as unverified until matched against the CBCG page.

description: No page in this slice was fetched directly; all candidates come from search-result evidence, so liveness, robots.txt posture and bot defences are unverified.

result.result_summary: Search returned consistent, plausible URLs across cbcg.me, europeanpaymentscouncil.eu, bancaditalia.it, worldbank.org, visasoutheasteurope.com, mastercard.rs.

why_it_matters: Corporate scheme sites (Visa/Mastercard) commonly sit behind Akamai/CDN bot protection; the deterministic verification pass should treat 403s there as bot-defended-but-live rather than dead.

description: No evidence found of an active Montenegrin startup-specific press-release wire or a national fintech-association newsroom that aggregates non-bank payment announcements. ICT Cortex is the closest substitute but is an ICT cluster, not a payments body.

result.result_summary: Searches in sr and en surfaced only general tech portals (Digitalizuj.Me, itspot.me) and the ICT Cortex blog; no dedicated fintech PR channel.

why_it_matters: Collection must rely on per-company crawling plus media relays, which raises miss-risk for very small launches.

description: Searched for regional challenger wallets (Aircash, KEKS Pay, Revolut, Monesa) entering or announcing Montenegro; results returned Croatian-market coverage only.

result.result_summary: No Montenegro-specific launch, licensing or press announcement for these wallets was found in this run — absence of evidence, not evidence of absence.

why_it_matters: Regional-challenger entry would be a major disruption vector for merchant acceptance; the gap should be closed by checking the CBCG e-money/payment-institution registers and each wallet's own newsroom directly.

description: Local-language coverage for merchant-side software was thin on some concepts: no established Montenegrin term surfaced for 'softPOS'/'tap-to-phone', and searches on 'QR plaćanje' returned mostly Serbian (RS) fiscal-receipt content rather than Montenegrin merchant QR schemes.

result.result_summary: sr queries on QR/merchant acceptance leaked heavily into the Serbian market; no ME-specific merchant QR scheme identified.

why_it_matters: Query glossary needs ME-specific disambiguators ('Crna Gora', '.me', 'CBCG', 'Podgorica') and English-in-local terms ('softPOS', 'tap to phone') to avoid RS/HR contamination.

description: The only funding-data aggregator found for ME fintech (Tracxn) lists ~102 entities dominated by forex/CFD and crypto shells domiciled in Montenegro (AMarkets, GANNMarkets, GoDefi, Impact, Prosecure) rather than domestic payment challengers.

result.result_summary: High entity count, low relevance density; only ~10 reported as funded.

why_it_matters: Naive use of the aggregator would badly distort the ME fintech actor map; every entry needs cross-validation against CBCG registers.

description: Several company homepages were inferred from organisation names rather than confirmed by a fetch in this run: logate.com, fleka.me, tehnopolis.me, and the 2bi.me root.

result.result_summary: URLs provided with moderate confidence; only prestopay.me was fetched directly this run.

why_it_matters: The downstream deterministic liveness pass must resolve these before they are treated as stable collection targets.

description: Fetch of https://cejn.gov.me/tenders returned no usable page content — no listing rows, no filters, no URLs.

result.result_summary: Hypothesis: the tender listing is client-side rendered or bot-defended, not dead. The domain is repeatedly cited as the live official portal by ujn.gov.me, gov.me and multiple aggregators, so it is recorded as unverified-but-almost-certainly-live, never as dead.

why_it_matters: The single most important source in this cell may need a headless browser or an internal JSON/API endpoint rather than a plain HTTP fetch; the collection design must budget for that.

description: Targeted local-language searches for concrete Montenegrin banking/payment procurement items ('POS terminal', 'platne kartice', 'bankarske usluge', 'bankomat') returned portal home pages and Bosnian/Serbian equivalents rather than actual ME notices.

result.result_summary: No individual Montenegrin banking-services or POS/card tender document was located through open web search in this run. The closest hits were a BiH treasury banking-services tender and BiH award notices on ejn.gov.ba — different jurisdiction, not usable for ME.

why_it_matters: Montenegrin notice text appears to be poorly indexed by general search engines (consistent with a JS-rendered portal). Item-level discovery will have to happen inside CEJN's own search, not via web search — a structural constraint on this workstream.

description: The procurement review commission does not live at the plausible-looking kzp.gov.me.

result.result_summary: Its decisions register is at kontrola-nabavki.me/rjesenja (admin instance at admin.kontrola-nabavki.me); contact email komisija@nabavka.gov.me. The guessed gov.me subdomain was not found.

why_it_matters: Illustrates that ME procurement institutions are scattered across gov.me, .me and .co.me domains; any seed list built by pattern-guessing gov.me subdomains will silently miss sources.

description: No Montenegro-specific banking or payment-services notice was retrievable from TED via general web search.

result.result_summary: Only TED's own explanatory pages and one EU Delegation security-services tender surfaced. Whether ME entities publish to TED at all (Montenegro is a candidate country, not an EU member) was not established in this run.

why_it_matters: TED's value for this cell may be limited to EU-Delegation/IPA contracts rather than national ME procurement; the collection plan should test this before investing in TED tooling.

description: The World Bank project id for the Montenegro Financial Infrastructure Modernization / SEPA (TIPS clone) operation was not confirmed against a project page.

result.result_summary: A 2025 disclosure PDF filename contains 'P509405', which is suggestive but not verified as this project's id. Recorded as a hypothesis, not a fact.

why_it_matters: The project id is the join key to the procurement plan and award data on Finances One; getting it wrong would silently pull the wrong pipeline.

description: No public vendor case study, reference page or go-live press release was found naming the core-banking platform of any Montenegrin bank (CKB, Hipotekarna, NLB Podgorica, Erste ME, Addiko ME, Lovćen, Prva banka, Universal Capital, Adriatic, Ziraat ME).

result.result_summary: Searches across generic core-banking vendor queries, bank-specific queries and named-vendor queries (Temenos, Oracle FLEXCUBE, Backbase, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR) returned zero ME core-banking references. Only ancillary systems (security, SoftPOS, e-banking, CRM, HR, data centre) surfaced.

why_it_matters: The core-banking layer is the highest-value procurement signal and it is invisible on the vendor side for ME. Coverage of this workstream must therefore lean on group-level parent disclosures (OTP, NLB, Erste, Addiko) and on bank T&C/app metadata fingerprints rather than vendor marketing.

description: No AML / financial-crime-compliance vendor was found publicly naming a Montenegrin bank as a customer.

result.result_summary: English-language searches on AML vendor + Montenegro returned only generic vendor-ranking listicles; no case study, press release or reference page named an ME institution.

why_it_matters: AML tooling is a mandated spend driven by MONEYVAL/EU-accession pressure, so the absence of vendor-side traces means this segment must be tracked via regulator (CBCG, Uprava za sprječavanje pranja novca) publications and bank annual reports instead of supplier marketing.

description: Local-language (sr/cnr) queries for AML vendor references were not productive because no ME-specific local vocabulary for AML product procurement surfaced in this pass.

result.result_summary: Local terms attempted for other subtopics (dobavljač, referenca, implementacija, saopštenje, ugovor, rješenje) worked well for ATM/POS, e-banking and integrator queries but the AML sweep was effectively English-only.

why_it_matters: Per the mandate, English-only coverage is a defect. A follow-up pass must run terms such as 'sprječavanje pranja novca', 'softver za usklađenost', 'monitoring transakcija', 'sankcione liste' against ME vendor and bank sites.

description: The Logate corporate URL (logate.com) was inferred from company identity rather than confirmed in a search result; the confirmed trace was a third-party profile on itkonekt.com.

result.result_summary: Bank references for Logate (contact centre at Lovćen banka and CKB) appear in secondary Montenegrin sources, not yet confirmed on a vendor-owned page in this pass.

why_it_matters: The vendor-owned reference page is the higher-credibility artefact and must be located and verified before the Lovćen/CKB contact-centre attribution is treated as established fact.

description: The available web search is US-biased and returned Wikipedia/bank-directory noise for many Montenegrin queries instead of vendor pages.

result.result_summary: Several sr-language queries returned generic bank profiles (thebanks.eu, Wikipedia, nomadcapitalist) rather than vendor references, indicating index thinness for the .me domain space.

why_it_matters: Vendor-side discovery for ME likely requires site-scoped crawling (site:printecgroup.com, site:payten.com, site:asee.* plus each .me vendor domain) rather than open-web querying; this changes the collection design for this cell.

description: No standalone, separately-published country-by-country reporting (CBCR) file naming Montenegro was located for any parent group in this run; CBCR appears only as an annex inside the group annual report PDF (Erste, Addiko, NLB as EU/CRD-scope institutions).

result.result_summary: Generic CRD IV CBCR explainers (KPMG, PwC trackers) surfaced instead of issuer-specific Montenegro tables.

why_it_matters: Collection must target the annual-report PDF annex by text search ('Montenegro', 'Crna Gora'), not a separate CBCR document endpoint.

description: Universal Capital Bank AD, Zapad banka AD, Prva banka Crne Gore and First Financial Bank were not tied to any listed foreign banking group with public consolidated IR reporting in the searches run.

result.result_summary: These appear locally/privately held or held by non-reporting owners; Adriatic Bank is described as linked to a US-based Adriatic Capital LLC with no traceable public IR site found.

why_it_matters: Cell #9 (foreign parent group reporting) simply cannot cover these banks - they must be picked up by local-disclosure cells, and the intel gap should be stated explicitly rather than assumed away.

description: Local-language (sr/me) searches for group-level quarterly presentations ('kvartalna prezentacija grupe', 'maticna banka konsolidovani izvjestaj') returned almost no parent-group material - only local subsidiary reports and CBCG pages.

result.result_summary: Parent groups publish group IR in EN (and HU/SL/DE/PL home languages); Montenegrin-language coverage exists only at subsidiary statutory level.

why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: for group-segment KPIs, English (plus HU/SL/PL home-market filings) is the operative language; sr/me collection should target subsidiary statutory statements for reconciliation only.

description: Earnings-call transcripts naming Montenegro are largely behind paywalls (Seeking Alpha, Quartr, Investing.com partial).

result.result_summary: Free access is limited to summaries and excerpts; issuer-hosted call decks and webcasts remain free.

why_it_matters: Budget for either a transcript licence or an ASR pipeline over issuer webcast audio if analyst-Q&A colour on Montenegro is required.

description: Some IR landing URLs were inferred from search-result domains rather than fetched in this pass (e.g. asee.io investor-relations path, ziraatbank.com.tr financials path, erstegroup financial-reports path).

result.result_summary: Document-level URLs returned by search are recorded in example_urls; landing pages are best-effort and unverified.

why_it_matters: The deterministic liveness pass must resolve these; a 403/404 here should trigger a site-search retry, not a dead-source verdict.

description: The expected domain 'ubcg.me' for the Association of Montenegrin Banks does not appear to exist; the association's actual site is ubcg.info.

result.result_summary: Local-language queries containing "ubcg.me" returned no association-owned page; a follow-up query surfaced ubcg.info/en/legislation/ and ubcg.info article paths.

why_it_matters: Any pipeline seeded with ubcg.me would record a false dead source and lose the most important association in the cell.

description: The Chamber of Economy's English-language committee paths under komora.me/en/cem/... appear in search results but returned HTTP 404 on fetch, while the Montenegrin paths under komora.me/komora/odbori/... resolved correctly.

result.result_summary: 404 on https://komora.me/en/cem/udruzenje-bankarstva-i-drugih-finansijskih-organizacija-i-osiguranja, /en/cem/udruzenja, /pkcg/odbori-udruzenja/ and /o-nama/publikacije/; success on https://komora.me/komora/odbori and its banking sub-page.

why_it_matters: The site has been restructured and the search index is stale; collectors must use the sr path scheme, which is also the authoritative one. Do not mark these as dead sources - the content exists under different URLs.

description: MFIC (Montenegrin Foreign Investors Council) blocks plain HTTP fetching.

result.result_summary: HTTP 403 Forbidden on both https://mfic.me/white-book/ and https://www.mfic.me/committees/committees; the same pages are indexed and referenced by third parties (CorD Magazine, Golden Group), so the site is live.

why_it_matters: The White Book is the highest-value position-paper series in this cell; a naive collector would classify it as dead. It needs a headless-browser or header-spoofing fetch path.

description: No published committee minutes were located for either the PKCG banking board or UBCG.

result.result_summary: The PKCG banking board page lists officers and 23 member representatives but carries no minutes, agendas or document links; UBCG publishes news items and the Bankar magazine rather than minutes.

why_it_matters: The 'committee minutes' element of this cell's mandate is not satisfiable directly; the practical substitutes are Glasnik session write-ups, PKCG announcements and trade-press coverage.

description: No standalone Montenegrin fintech or payment-services association was found.

result.result_summary: Local-language searches for an IKT/fintech association returned ICT Cortex (a general tech cluster), IT klaster Crne Gore, the newly formed CFO Asocijacija, and a 2022 UNDP regulatory assessment of the fintech framework - but no fintech trade body. Fintech coordination instead happens through CBCG + ICT Cortex + UBCG joint events (FinTech hackathon, sandbox discussions).

why_it_matters: Payment-industry positions in ME must be tracked through the banking association and the tech cluster jointly; there is no single fintech lobby to monitor.

description: Montenegro Business Alliance (MBA) has no located live official website.

result.result_summary: Only third-party organisation records (DevelopmentAid, WBC-RTI, directory listings) and dated news items were found; no mba.* or similar own domain surfaced.

why_it_matters: MBA may be dormant or absorbed; treating it as an active association would produce a permanently empty collection target.
